advisor.name: Advisor
advisor.description: Advisors are Force-sensitive counselors who work through other people instead of seeking authority themselves. Some avoid leadership because they distrust what power would make of them; others find their advice more useful spread across many worlds than spent on one. They read a situation's risks quickly and steer the people in it toward a better outcome. The same instincts make an excellent con artist, which every Advisor is careful to remember.

advocate.name: Advocate
advocate.description: Advocates are political operators who win arguments rather than elections. They turn an opponent's words back on him, rescue an ally's careless remark, and apply pressure where a speech would fail. Most work behind a more personable figure, writing the lines and deciding which fight is worth having. A good one is a mentor; a great one can be mentor or rival as the moment requires.

aggressor.name: Aggressor
aggressor.description: Aggressors fight to make surrender the obvious choice. They are brutally durable combatants who use terror deliberately, convincing enemies that fighting is worse than backing down. Many prefer to end a confrontation without killing, striking with just enough force to break resolve. Others come to enjoy the fear they cause, which is the beginning of a longer fall.

agitator.name: Agitator
agitator.description: Agitators turn frightened populations into ones willing to fight. The Empire rules through fear, and an Agitator's work is replacing that fear with anger, courage, or plain stubbornness. Most come to it through personal loss, and understand crowds, streets, and when to bully a bully. Alliance command treats them as a necessary evil, aware that civilians who rise up untrained tend to die in numbers.

alchemist.name: Alchemist
alchemist.description: Alchemists pour the Force into objects, crafting talismans, medicines, and weapons that behave as though they were alive. The Jedi Order never embraced the practice, and the traditions that did run through the Sith, the Nightsisters, and older cults, so few remain to warn a student away. Most Alchemists work in medicine, where the flow of a remedy through a body most resembles the Force itself.

ambassador.name: Ambassador
ambassador.description: Ambassadors bring planets, systems, and corporations over to a cause, and keep them there. They are masters of the bargaining table who never enter a negotiation without room to move, and their real skill is making the other side feel the agreement was its own idea. The Alliance lives on their results: every world convinced means more hope and more resources.

analyst.name: Analyst
analyst.description: Analysts turn raw information into the intelligence that decides battles and negotiations. They parse and remember enormous volumes of data, then find the connection that makes it useful, whether a troop-movement pattern, a local custom, or an Imperial code. Some specialise in a single subject; others act as liaisons to commanders and politicians who need an answer immediately.

arbiter.name: Arbiter
arbiter.description: Arbiters step between enemies and find the misunderstanding underneath the fight. They read the pressures running through a conflict and the fault lines that keep it alive, then talk both sides toward something they can live with. An Arbiter reaches for discussion first and a lightsaber last, while keeping the wider picture in view: peace is the goal, though not always the nearest one.

arc_trooper.name: ARC Trooper
arc_trooper.description: Advanced Recon Commandos — the Grand Army's elite. Where standard clones follow orders, ARC Troopers are trained to think creatively and act independently, taking the missions no one else can: infiltration, jetpack insertions, quick strikes behind enemy lines. Command considers them the best of the best.

archaeologist.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist.description: Archaeologists hunt the galaxy's lost civilizations and unlock what they left behind. The work is scholarly and physical in equal measure, since ruins are rarely near anywhere safe. Most care little who governs, except where policy touches their digs, and the Empire's appetite for revised history pushes many to work outside official channels entirely.

armorer.name: Armorer
armorer.description: Armorers survive through ingenuity and stubbornness rather than reflexes. Where other Guardians deflect or evade, an Armorer builds a better defense and reinforces it with the Force, eventually producing armor that can turn a lightsaber. They work as readily on a battlefield with scavenged parts as in a machine shop, which matters when the Empire hounds every step a Force user takes.

artisan.name: Artisan
artisan.description: Artisans feel the Force in the tools they hold and the things they build, and use that connection to make objects of unusual precision. They do not turn out identical goods; each piece is individual, and some approach art. The path often finds people raised among machines who never learn what their instincts really are. They simply notice that broken things explain themselves.

ascetic.name: Ascetic
ascetic.description: Ascetics withdraw from comfort to sharpen the mind, judging their worth by their understanding of the Force rather than anything they own. Long spells on the fringes leave them able to make do with almost nothing and hard to rattle, if sometimes rusty in company. Many emerge from isolation because something in the galaxy's balance disturbed them enough to act.

assassin.name: Assassin
assassin.description: Where most Bounty Hunters bring a target in alive, Assassins are hired to end them. They prefer to arrive quietly, work at whatever range the job allows, and leave before anyone knows they came. Despite the trade they keep the profession's ethics: no needless bloodshed, contracts honoured exactly. Some treat the work with something close to reverence, others are simply comfortable being cold.

ataru_striker.name: Ataru Striker
ataru_striker.description: Ataru Strikers resolve fights quickly, because a long fight is a losing one when help is far away. The form commits the whole body to the attack, using athleticism and terrain to strike from angles an opponent cannot cover. It demands complete confidence and leaves little defense beyond sheer offense, so an enemy who survives the opening flurry becomes the real danger.

beast_rider.name: Beast Rider
beast_rider.description: Beast Riders break and train wild mounts, then get results from them no vehicle could manage on the same ground. Plenty of worlds are too poor, too cold, or too rough for repulsorlifts, and a creature that evolved there needs neither filters nor fuel. Rebel commands often post them as scouts, since tracks left by an animal draw far less Imperial attention than tyre marks.

big_game_hunter.name: Big-Game Hunter
big_game_hunter.description: Big-Game Hunters seek out the galaxy's most dangerous animals and fight them on purpose. They respect the environments they work in without being especially curious about them; what matters is what waits at the end. Many take contracts thinning a herd or removing a creature that has become a threat to a settlement, and most will tell you it counts as a public service.

bodyguard.name: Bodyguard
bodyguard.description: Bodyguards keep people and places intact, and they are the right person to stand behind when shooting starts. They handle weapons of most sizes, watch their surroundings constantly, and drive well enough to get a client out. Work is easy to find in the Outer Rim, particularly for anyone untroubled by who is paying. In a group they are usually the heaviest combatant present.

charmer.name: Charmer
charmer.description: Charmers get what they want by asking for it well. Where a Politico rallies and a Scoundrel threatens, a Charmer flatters, and convinces the other party that giving in was their own good idea. The approach opens doors that force would only close, and it holds up in a fight as well, since an opponent made to doubt himself lowers his guard.

clone_commander.name: Clone Commander
clone_commander.description: Clones bred and trained to lead. A commander directs a regiment on the Jedi's behalf — weighing strategy, logistics, and the lives of their brothers, advising when they can and executing when ordered. As the saying goes, 'If the droids don't get me, the paperwork will.'

clone_officer.name: Clone Officer
clone_officer.description: Clone Officers carry every level of responsibility in the Grand Army short of the highest. The role runs from sergeants who know each trooper in their squad by name to commanders directing full regiments under a Jedi general. An officer has to recognise trouble early, stay calm in front of the ranks, and appear to have anticipated everything, whether or not that is true.

clone_pilot.name: Clone Pilot
clone_pilot.description: Every clone can fly something. Clone Pilots are the ones trained to do it under fire, serving in Republic Navy squadrons flying Headhunters, Torrents, and ARC-170s, or running troops through contested air in transports. Assignments change often, so training covers a wide spread of craft, and some clone pilots spend the whole war in walkers and speeders without seeing space.

clone_trooper.name: Clone Trooper
clone_trooper.description: Clone Troopers are the Grand Army's infantry, and the standard against which its whole capability is measured. The role covers a wide spread of jobs, from cold assault and SCUBA work to paratroopers, flame troopers, and medics, and troopers showing a particular aptitude are pulled out for advanced training. Within a squad, individuals take the heavy weapon, the explosives, or the medpac as the mission needs.

clone_veteran.name: Clone Veteran
clone_veteran.description: The soldier no training program can manufacture, forged instead by firsthand battle. Veterans read the enemy, survive any biome, and pass hard-won lessons to green 'shinies' — often holding low rank by choice, to serve alongside their brothers on the field rather than above them.

colossus.name: Colossus
colossus.description: A Colossus outlasts opponents rather than out-fighting them, carrying scar tissue that would have killed most combatants several times over. The approach draws on stoic traditions older than the Jedi Order: pain passes, and a fighter can rise above it. Some reach that state through meditation and focus, others by feeding on the pain itself, which is a shorter road to the dark side.

commando.name: Commando
commando.description: Commandos hit the enemy where it is not looking, and get home afterwards. They find a target, disable it, survive the response, and extract, usually as part of a small team used like a surgical instrument. Since standing battles are a losing proposition for the Alliance, commandos inflict a disproportionate share of the damage the Rebellion actually manages.

commodore.name: Commodore
commodore.description: Commodores command the Alliance's capital ships, and every one of those is scarce enough that the posting is a statement of trust. The work is equal parts navigation, resource management, and nerve, and the best of them end up directing whole fleets against Imperial counterparts with far greater tonnage. They spend almost no time planetside, and prefer it that way.

courier.name: Courier
courier.description: Couriers move stolen intelligence to the people who can use it, usually straight through Imperial checkpoints. The work is a specialised kind of smuggling in which the cargo is information, and many Couriers learned it running goods before the war. Some keep a steady route and a durable cover story; others improvise every trip and rely on speed and nerve.

cyber_tech.name: Cyber Tech
cyber_tech.description: Cyber Techs build, fit, and maintain cybernetics, treating the body as one more machine that can be repaired and improved. Most carry a good deal of their own work. How far they take it depends on culture and conviction, since some societies find heavy augmentation unremarkable and others treat it as taboo, and a Cyber Tech usually has opinions about both.

death_watch_warrior.name: Death Watch Warrior
death_watch_warrior.description: Mandalorian militants who reject their homeworld's peace and long for a return to warrior conquest. Allied with the Separatists, they wage hit-and-run sabotage — surgical jetpack strikes on outposts, power plants, and defenses — trading compromise for victory. To the Death Watch, mercy is weakness and battle is birthright.

demolitionist.name: Demolitionist
demolitionist.description: Demolitionists understand explosions well enough to stand near them. They set everything from a grenade on a tripwire to timed and proximity charges, and they know where on a structure a small charge does the work of a large one. The job punishes a single mistake, so most cultivate a steady head, and a group that keeps one tends to watch him closely.

doctor.name: Doctor
doctor.description: Doctors are never short of work in the Outer Rim, though much of it involves patching up people who earned their injuries. They bring broad knowledge and steady nerves along with medical skill, and many took the job to see more of the galaxy than a medical school allows. In a group the Doctor becomes the combat medic, which makes him popular very quickly.

driver.name: Driver
driver.description: Drivers move people and cargo once the ship is down, and the gap between a Driver and anyone who can operate a speeder shows the moment the weather turns or the shooting starts. They understand their machines and handle them with some style. Companies, militaries, governments, and criminals all need the skill, and a few Outer Rim worlds will pay to watch it raced.

droid_specialist.name: Droid Specialist
droid_specialist.description: Alliance Droid Specialists keep droids fighting rather than restoring them to factory condition, since there is rarely the time or the stock for anything better. Their charges arrive mismatched and leave patched, and how well a base is supplied can be read off its droids alone. Most grow protective of them, whether they see sentients or valuable machines.

droid_tech.name: Droid Tech
droid_tech.description: Droid Techs build, repair, and get results out of droids better than anyone. On the fringe droids do much of the labour and are maintained badly, which keeps a Droid Tech busy, and the most skilled build custom units from nothing. The other half of the job is persuasion, since plenty of droids are capricious, difficult, or simply too useful to switch off.

enforcer.name: Enforcer
enforcer.description: Enforcers know that results rarely require violence, because the credible promise of it usually does the job. They fight well enough when it comes to that, but they work by intimidation, leverage, and a genuine grasp of how criminal organisations operate. Syndicates use them as muscle and as a public face at once, and a good Enforcer can talk a group out of a fight it would have lost.

entrepreneur.name: Entrepreneur
entrepreneur.description: Entrepreneurs invest in the future and expect to own a piece of it. They open markets nobody had noticed, on the assumption that any problem yields to a large enough credit line. Rules written by established competitors strike them as obstacles rather than law, though they are careful rather than reckless about it. Every group benefits from one, if only for the contacts and the funding.

executioner.name: Executioner
executioner.description: Executioners end fights in a single exchange. Seekers often work alone in hostile places where a wounded enemy is a problem that compounds, and Executioners answer that by making the first strike final. Deciding who warrants that treatment is the harder part of the work, and the judgement involved is exactly where the dark side finds an opening.

figurehead.name: Figurehead
figurehead.description: Figureheads lead through reputation rather than rank. Most come from civilian life and stand outside the Alliance chain of command entirely, relying on political connections, personal history, and nerve to move people. Their strength is endurance in public: a Figurehead carries the fears of everyone watching and cannot be seen to falter. Mon Mothma and Bail Organa are the examples everyone reaches for.

force_adherent.name: Force Adherent
force_adherent.description: Force Adherents order their lives around the Force whether or not they can touch it. Belief is not confined to the Jedi; the Lasat honour the Ashla and the Bogan, and Gand findsmen use techniques outsiders read as Force work. Adherents keep rituals, make pilgrimages to places like Jedha, and train hard, and those who pursue it earnestly find real strength even without sensitivity.

force_sensitive_emergent.name: Force Sensitive Emergent
force_sensitive_emergent.description: Force-Sensitive Emergents are untrained talents who have only begun to notice what they can do. The Rebellion shelters a number of them, and while few will ever meet an actual Jedi, the Alliance is one of the last places where the Order's traditions are discussed openly. Awareness often arrives late in life, which is why this path can begin at any point rather than only at the start.

force_sensitive_exile.name: Force Sensitive Exile
force_sensitive_exile.description: Force-Sensitive Exiles survived the purge by disappearing. The Empire treats using the Force as a capital crime, but the galaxy is too large to search completely and Order 66 concentrated on the Jedi themselves. An Exile might be a fled Padawan or a child hidden by family. Either way the last decades were spent staying quiet, so their abilities run to concealment and control rather than display.

force_sensitive_outcast.name: Force-Sensitive Outcast
force_sensitive_outcast.description: Force-Sensitive Outcasts answer to neither the Jedi nor the Sith. Some trained under one and left, by choice or expulsion; others were never found at all. They survive at the edges of Republic and Separatist space, self-taught and unpredictable, and their fighting usually assembles half-remembered forms with whatever else has worked. Lightsabers change hands more often than the Order likes to admit.

fringer.name: Fringer
fringer.description: Fringers know how to find what they need and how to reach where they are going. Part negotiator and part astrogator, they are comfortable well beyond the Core and tend to be the one a group sends into a strange starport to arrange things. Many are capable pilots, and almost all are harder to catch or hit than they look.

gadgeteer.name: Gadgeteer
gadgeteer.description: Gadgeteers solve the Bounty Hunter's basic problem, which is that a quarry usually has friends. They present themselves as a one-person assault force using the newest equipment and a good deal of personal modification, and they combine that with genuine technical skill. For a small team the combination of technician and combatant is often exactly what is missing.

gambler.name: Gambler
gambler.description: Gamblers know the games, but their real skill is reading the people playing them. Body language, voice, and habit tell a Gambler when to move, and a fixed expression tells the table nothing in return. The same instincts work well away from a sabacc board, whether the stakes are a cargo price or talking an armed thug into a better mood.

general.name: General
general.description: The Clone Wars turned the Jedi from independent troubleshooters into generals of the Grand Army. A Jedi General leads from the field, carrying the strategy, logistics, and administration of war while fighting beside their troops — bound to protect civilians first, the Republic second, and their soldiers last, never losing sight that the true goal is peace.

gunner.name: Gunner
gunner.description: Gunners treat a vehicle's weapons as the clearest expression of what one person can do to the Empire. They work turrets, cannons, and anything else mounted, and they consider themselves responsible for everyone riding with them. The role attracts people who can hold their nerve against unknown odds, and who find the destruction of a target reward enough on its own.

gunslinger.name: Gunslinger
gunslinger.description: Gunslingers are the best shots in the Outer Rim and see little reason to hide it. Life on the frontier rewards a fast draw, and a Gunslinger's reputation tends to arrive before he does, which brings both work and challengers. Between jobs they take whatever the Rim offers, from freight to smuggling, and they stay one step ahead of whatever passes for local law.

healer.name: Healer
healer.description: Healers use the Force to fuel the body's own recovery, sometimes turning an injury that should have been fatal into one a patient survives. They treat the spirit alongside the body, on the view that helping one person matters as much as helping a civilization. Many hold strong objections to violence, having spent their lives undoing it, so few develop much in the way of combat ability.

heavy.name: Heavy
heavy.description: Heavies carry the largest weapons a person can carry and usually have the build to match. The role is straightforward: bring overwhelming firepower, stand where it counts, and absorb what comes back. Lugging that much hardware builds the endurance the job needs, and the mere sight of it often ends an argument before it starts. In a group, a Heavy fills the role of a light tank.

hermit.name: Hermit
hermit.description: Hermits take Seeker self-reliance to its conclusion and live apart, developing their connection to the Force without interruption. Some are avoiding debts, bounties, or a former uniform; others simply want to concentrate. Long isolation makes them formidable in the wild, unusually attuned to animals, and perfectly capable in a fight, since nothing about surviving alone out there is gentle.

hotshot.name: Hotshot
hotshot.description: Hotshots fly on instinct and improvise the rest. Where an Ace relies on technique, a Hotshot takes the opening the moment it appears and worries about consequences later, which produces both the Rebellion's best flying and most of its losses. The Alliance has no shortage of young pilots in this mould and very few old ones, and it tends to retire the survivors into training commands.

hunter.name: Hunter
hunter.description: Hunters track and kill the predators that threaten settled life, and their connection to the Force helps them tell a dangerous animal from a malicious one. They work quietly, at range where possible, and move through terrain that would stop anyone else. The same instincts apply to sentient quarry, which most Hunters consider the more dangerous work.

imperial_academy_cadet.name: Imperial Academy Cadet
imperial_academy_cadet.description: Imperial Academy Cadets trained to serve the Empire and left before they finished. The academies promise order, advancement, and a way off a quiet world, and that promise holds until a cadet is asked to practise suppressing civilians. Those who walk out bring something valuable with them: Imperial tactics, protocols, and hardware learned from the inside, all of it now a liability for their old employers.

infiltrator.name: Infiltrator
infiltrator.description: Infiltrators are what most people picture when they hear the word spy. They talk or sneak their way into the places that matter, gather what they came for, and get out, usually without backup and often without a planned exit. They favour quiet, close work over confrontation, and the Alliance increasingly attaches them to strike teams so that a raid gathers intelligence as well as causing damage.

instructor.name: Instructor
instructor.description: Instructors exist so that recruits reach a battlefield already knowing what to do. Handing someone a blaster and pointing them at a war wastes lives the Rebellion cannot spare, so an Instructor drills weapon handling, discipline, and enough field medicine that a squad can keep itself alive. Most are combat-capable themselves, since the Alliance rarely has the luxury of teachers who only teach.

interrogator.name: Interrogator
interrogator.description: Interrogators recover the information nobody wrote down, sometimes from subjects who do not know they have it. The best of them prepare thoroughly, since personal history is what provides leverage, and then choose a technique to suit the person. Physical methods work on some and harden others, and Imperial officers are trained against them, so the most effective interrogations are social rather than violent.

investigator.name: Investigator
investigator.description: Investigators work out who did it, and do it to honour the victims rather than to satisfy their own curiosity. Violent crime leaves an impression in the Force, and an Investigator can read those impressions the way another reads a room, which makes them something like a physician for a damaged community. The cost is exposure: constant proximity to suffering wears down even steady people.

juyo_berserker.name: Juyo Berserker
juyo_berserker.description: Juyo Berserkers fight with the seventh lightsaber form, the one the old Order restricted to a handful it trusted. The style runs on genuine fury and produces fast, unpredictable, overwhelming attacks, which is exactly why it was watched so closely. Some practitioners hide the emotion driving it behind perfect calm; others let it show. Either way, defense is nearly an afterthought.

knight.name: Knight
knight.description: A Jedi Knight is warrior, diplomat, and symbol at once, leading clone troopers through a war the Order never wanted. Knights are the Republic's most visible face, more so than its senators, and they routinely decide who risks dying for it. Detachment keeps that judgement clear, but too much of it reduces lives to figures in a casualty report. Requires Force Rating 2 or higher.

magus.name: Magus
magus.description: A Magus assembles rituals, relics, and forbidden texts into a personal route to the Force. The Jedi avoided this kind of experiment and there is nobody left to discourage it, which is exactly the danger: without oversight, a Magus is free to reach for power that reaches back. Most seek not just knowledge but control, on the reasoning that anything running through everything can be pushed.

makashi_duelist.name: Makashi Duelist
makashi_duelist.description: Makashi Duelists win by presence as much as by blade work. The form was built to fight other lightsabers, and it relies on poise, precision, and control so complete that an opponent never sees strain. Detractors call it vain and miss the point: the flourishes exist to frustrate and exhaust, and the duelist waits for the moment that exhaustion opens.

marauder.name: Marauder
marauder.description: Marauders would rather close the distance than shoot, and they are usually the toughest thing in the fight once they do. They take a great deal of punishment and return more, which makes them excellent at intimidation as well as at combat. Some come from worlds where advanced weapons were never an option; others come from cultures that consider melee the only honourable way to settle anything.

marshal.name: Marshal
marshal.description: Marshals keep order where there is little government to help them. They are good at getting information out of witnesses and confessions out of suspects, and equally comfortable ending an argument with a blaster if talking fails. On the frontier a Marshal's word often is the law, and knowing the local criminals by name is most of the job.

martial_artist.name: Martial Artist
martial_artist.description: Martial Artists fight without needing a weapon, drawing on combat traditions developed across the galaxy over centuries. Some trained formally in a school with a philosophy attached; others learned in the field and disgraced themselves leaving. Precision matters more than strength, and the discipline that produces it also teaches when a fight is worth having at all.

mechanic.name: Mechanic
mechanic.description: Mechanics are either the glue holding everything together or the grease making it go, and most would say both before returning to work. Good ones are hard to find and trustworthy ones harder, which is why captains will cross systems for a Mechanic they know. Those who take ship work want to see the galaxy, and they tend to pick up enough improvisation to handle trouble that is not mechanical.

medic.name: Medic
medic.description: The Alliance cannot trade casualties with the Empire, so every soldier it keeps alive counts twice. Medics exist to make that arithmetic work, treating anyone in the unit regardless of species and staying functional while everyone around them panics. Most are not pacifists. They would rather save a life than take one, but will take one to save another.

mercenary_soldier.name: Mercenary Soldier
mercenary_soldier.description: Mercenary Soldiers are the warfare specialists among Hired Guns, as comfortable directing a fight as fighting it. Most served in a real military first and held some rank there, which shows in their grasp of tactics and their personal discipline. Give one a force to lead and the danger multiplies; even without one, a Mercenary Soldier tends to end up in charge when shooting starts.

modder.name: Modder
modder.description: Modders would rather improve a machine than build one. They tinker constantly, and if the crew's gear keeps getting taken apart and reassembled slightly better, a Modder is responsible. Specialising in generalising lets them work across weapons, ships, droids, and personal kit alike, and a team with one aboard gets upgrades and attachments it would otherwise never see.

navigator.name: Navigator
navigator.description: Navigators care about the route as much as the destination. They chart hyperspace lanes and overland passages with an accuracy that can look like luck to anyone watching, and they are usually decent pilots who simply find arriving safely more interesting than firepower. Left alone they will keep shaving distance off a known route purely because a solved problem bores them.

nightsister.name: Nightsister
nightsister.description: Dathomirian witches who wield the Force through alchemy and magick, drawing power from their world's ichor and its strange creatures. Neither serene like the Jedi nor consumed by rage like the Sith, the Nightsisters freely cross the line between light and dark — collecting power, bending every tool to their clan's survival, and thriving in conflict.

niman_disciple.name: Niman Disciple
niman_disciple.description: Niman Disciples are negotiators who accept that talks sometimes fail. They train with the lightsaber for that eventuality, concentrating on defense and survival rather than attack, and they integrate the Force into the fighting more than most Consulars do. The point is never to win the fight; it is to still be standing when the conversation can resume.

operator.name: Operator
operator.description: Operators run their pursuits from a cockpit, because nothing on foot outruns a speeder or a starship. They keep a target in sight through manoeuvres most pilots would not attempt and disable it rather than destroy it, since a bounty is worth nothing as debris. Many work alone with only a ship for company; others ferry a team in and provide cover while it works.

outlaw_tech.name: Outlaw Tech
outlaw_tech.description: Outlaw Techs build the things nobody will sell you. A blaster pushed past its tolerances, a transponder that swears a smuggler's freighter is a pilgrimage vessel, a protocol droid with an unusual subroutine: the answer is usually yes, for a price. The Outer Rim suits them, since the work attracts less official attention there and the customers appreciate it more.

padawan.name: Padawan
padawan.description: A Padawan is an apprentice, and the title describes a way of thinking as much as a rank. Once an initiate earns a kyber crystal and builds a lightsaber, they are assigned to a Knight or Master, and in wartime that means acting as runner, aide, and sometimes lieutenant. The braid marks the attachment and is cut when training ends. Knights and Masters occasionally take the title up again deliberately.

padawan_survivor.name: Padawan Survivor
padawan_survivor.description: Padawan Survivors are the handful of apprentices who lived through Order 66 and the hunts that followed. Their training stopped abruptly and most had little field experience, so they entered a hostile galaxy young, unprepared, and alone. Survival usually meant no-questions work or outright crime, and revealing what they could do generally cost them whoever they had just saved.

pathfinder.name: Pathfinder
pathfinder.description: Pathfinders explore ground nobody has surveyed and come back. They live off the land for months at a stretch with minimal supplies, often alongside an animal companion, and some bond with those companions through the Force closely enough to borrow their senses. Many grew up on primitive worlds where knowing the wilderness was simply how a community survived.

peacekeeper.name: Peacekeeper
peacekeeper.description: Peacekeepers step into wars to protect the people caught in them, and enforce a settlement at the tip of a lightsaber when nothing else will hold. They recognise threats early and delegate well, keeping themselves for the problems only they can handle. Most take the role after being pushed into authority repeatedly, out of responsibility rather than any appetite for command.

performer.name: Performer
performer.description: Performers need the room's attention and know several ways to take it. They lie with more conviction than a politician and charm better than most diplomats, and the acrobats and dancers among them are in genuinely dangerous physical condition. A Performer can hold a crowd while the rest of the group works, and can generally handle themselves once the crowd notices.

pilot.name: Pilot
pilot.description: A Pilot stops treating the ship as equipment. They coax performance out of tired transports that the specifications say is impossible, and given time and parts will turn one into something genuinely fast. Work is never scarce, and a group discovers exactly what a Pilot is worth during its first real space battle.

pirate.name: Pirate
pirate.description: Pirates take what they can reach and are honest about it, at least among themselves. They raid well-stocked ships, sell what they lift, and rely on reputation to avoid fighting for it more often than not. Some end up helping rebel cells, since desperate cells have few legal options and Pirates know how to live outside the law. Whether that becomes loyalty is anyone's guess.

politico.name: Politico
politico.description: Politicos talk, and they do it better than anyone else in the room. What another achieves through force, a Politico manages with the right words and a workable plan, whether that means inspiring a crowd or dismantling an opponent's confidence in public. Ambition is the constant; they will work for someone else temporarily but never comfortably.

propagandist.name: Propagandist
propagandist.description: Propagandists shape what the galaxy believes about the war. Sometimes that means releasing a truth the Empire buried, and sometimes it means a fabrication that demoralises a garrison, and few Propagandists are troubled by the difference. The Rebellion needs ordinary people to think resistance is possible, and that belief is manufactured as deliberately as any weapon.

prophet.name: Prophet
prophet.description: Prophets speak to crowds rather than individuals, offering hope and a reason to keep going. Medium hardly matters, whether a sermon, a HoloNet posting, a stack of tracts, or a hijacked transmission, so long as the message spreads. Their glimpses of the Cosmic Force arrive as images that must be translated into ordinary language, and something is always lost or added in the telling.

protector.name: Protector
protector.description: Protectors put themselves between danger and the people who cannot handle it, and few things get through their guard. They carry enough medical knowledge to stabilise the injuries they fail to prevent, and they usually work at scale rather than guarding one individual, acting as rescue workers or shepherding refugees out of a collapsing situation.

quartermaster.name: Quartermaster
quartermaster.description: Quartermasters make sure the food, ammunition, and medical supplies arrive where they are needed, which is among the hardest jobs in any military. A campaign that outruns its supply lines stops being a campaign. The Alliance grants them wide latitude in how they source things, and the better ones make regular use of it at the expense of criminals and the Empire alike.

racer.name: Racer
racer.description: Racers compete on anything that moves and use the Force to know where they are in a way instruments cannot manage. Obstacles register as something closer to shadows in space and time, which lets a Racer take a line nobody else would attempt. As the sense develops it extends to other people, so a Racer becomes uncannily good at being where someone else is about to be.

recruit.name: Recruit
recruit.description: The Recruit specialization is basic Alliance military training, open to a character from any career. The Rebellion is not an army in the Imperial mold, but it teaches its people to move under fire, handle a weapon, and survive long enough to finish the job. Diplomats and scientists take it as readily as soldiers do, because a treaty is worth nothing if the negotiator never comes home.

republic_navy_officer.name: Republic Navy Officer
republic_navy_officer.description: Republic Navy Officers provide the strategic judgement the Grand Army lacks. Drawn from scattered system defence fleets, they arrived with wildly different training and one thing in common: they can outthink an opponent, whether that is a single warship or an entire invasion. Jedi generals rely on them heavily, since fighting a war is not what the Order trained anyone to do.

republic_representative.name: Republic Representative
republic_representative.description: Republic Representatives are junior members of the Galactic Senate, sent to speak for a population or party their world's Senator cannot cover alone. They sit on committees and receive the same briefings as a full Senator, and they stand in when one is absent, but they cannot introduce legislation or vote. The work keeps them travelling far more than a Senator's does, which leaves them unusually well connected away from Coruscant.

retired_clone_trooper.name: Retired Clone Trooper
retired_clone_trooper.description: Clone troopers were grown on Kamino from Jango Fett's genetic template, trained for war from decanting, and decommissioned once their accelerated aging outpaced their usefulness. The handful still alive carry Republic training that the Empire's stormtroopers never received, along with a share of the guilt for Order 66. Some fight the Empire out of anger, some out of shame, and some because soldiering is the only work they know.
retired_clone_trooper.restriction_note: Only human male characters may take this specialization (Dawn of Rebellion p.108).

rigger.name: Rigger
rigger.description: Riggers refuse to fly anything stock. They add, tune, and rebuild until their vehicle outperforms its class and carries at least one surprise the enemy has not accounted for. Given how outnumbered Rebel pilots usually are, that margin matters, and Riggers post the best survival rates among the Alliance's Aces. Most also keep useful friends in the outlaw tech community.

saboteur.name: Saboteur
saboteur.description: Saboteurs make sure the enemy cannot use what it has. Denying the Empire its vehicles, weapons, and networks requires understanding them thoroughly enough to stop them permanently, which makes a Saboteur a technician first and a covert operative second. Explosives are the obvious method and rarely the only one, and timing usually matters more than the charge.

sage.name: Sage
sage.description: Sages hold that understanding is the most reliable form of power, in a negotiation as much as on a battlefield. They study a situation until they can see what everyone in it actually wants, then use that to change minds. The belief underneath is that hatred is mostly ignorance, and that a being who understands another's reasons finds compassion easier than contempt.

sapper.name: Sapper
sapper.description: Sappers build what the Alliance needs and destroy what the Empire relies on, which are closer to the same skill than it sounds. They site and construct bases, then scout enemy fortifications for the cracks that a well-placed charge will open. The work is dangerous three times over: getting close, setting the charge, and often joining the assault afterwards.

scavenger.name: Scavenger
scavenger.description: Scavengers make a living off what the war leaves behind. A battlefield full of wrecked droids, unstable munitions, and half-disabled equipment deters most people, which is exactly why the pay is better than anything else on offer. Most work alone, improvise constantly, and occasionally turn up something far older than the Republic underneath the recent wreckage.

scholar.name: Scholar
scholar.description: A Scholar among fringers looks absurd until the group meets something it does not recognise. Broad knowledge and a habit of paying attention solve problems that tracking and firepower cannot, and even criminal bosses keep someone clever around when expanding an operation. Most Scholars in the field are there because the field is where the questions are.

scientist.name: Scientist
scientist.description: The Alliance solves problems with ingenuity because it cannot solve them with resources, and Scientists are where that ingenuity comes from. They cover supply, shelter, transport, weapons, and defences, and while command prefers to keep them well behind the line, plenty insist on testing their own work where it will be used. Some signed on specifically to fight.

scoundrel.name: Scoundrel
scoundrel.description: Scoundrels are part con artist, part gunfighter, part cantina brawler, and reliably quick into trouble. Rules interest them only where one can be turned to advantage, and luck is something they believe in with more confidence than the evidence supports. In a group a Scoundrel is the all-purpose option: a passable face, a decent shot, and a source of ideas nobody else would suggest.

scout.name: Scout
scout.description: Finding a planet is one thing; walking around on it and learning what it holds is another. Scouts survey unknown worlds with scanners and judgement, and the nerve involved is easy to underestimate. They know how to cover ground, find food and shelter, and gather what a mission needs, and most fly atmospheric craft well. Independents work with looser oversight than corporate survey teams and prefer it.

seer.name: Seer
seer.description: Seers stay aware of the Force constantly, reading meaning into ripples most Force users never notice. The problem is volume: a crowded world produces more signal than anyone can sort, so many Seers live apart simply to hear clearly. From that distance they often catch an event before it happens and send word to whoever is close enough to act.

senator.name: Senator
senator.description: A politician who fights with words as weapons and shields, on either side of the war. Commanding a squad of diplomats and staff, a Senator advances their homeworld's interests through rhetoric, coalition, and — when needed — obfuscation and spywork, all while navigating a fractured government and a relentless enemy.

sentry.name: Sentry
sentry.description: Sentries protect neighbourhoods rather than systems. While other Sentinels take the long view, a Sentry patrols streets and alleys for the people nobody else counts, and considers a crime already committed to be a failure. The old Order thought them too attached to individuals; Sentries channelled the grief and anger that came with that attachment and kept working.

separatist_commander.name: Separatist Commander
separatist_commander.description: The CIS draws its officers from everywhere — patriots, corporate soldiers, militia leaders, even tactical droids — long on daring and improvisation, short on experience. A Separatist Commander juggles fleets, troops, logistics, and Separatist politics, turning patchwork armies and surprise technology into victories the Republic's stolid methods can't anticipate.

shadow.name: Shadow
shadow.description: Shadows hunted the Sith when the Jedi still believed the Sith were extinct. Now the roles are reversed: a Dark Lord governs the galaxy and the Shadows are the ones hiding. They pursue dark side users and untouchable criminals through methods of questionable character, on the reasoning that the target justifies the tools, which is a line they have to watch carefully.

sharpshooter.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter.description: Sharpshooters are the masters of personal-scale ranged combat, and the most valuable person present once shooting starts. They stay composed under fire, take their time, and remove threats with unhurried efficiency. Some work as snipers from concealment; others prefer to stand with the squad and lay down the volume. Most favour a single heavily personalised weapon.

shien_expert.name: Shien Expert
shien_expert.description: Shien Experts hold two ideas about a lightsaber at once: it overpowers an opponent's guard, and it turns blaster fire back on whoever sent it. The form needs cunning as much as strength, and its practitioners prepare battlefields well before a fight, studying locations on arrival and setting up what the terrain allows. A long engagement favours them.

shii_cho_knight.name: Shii-Cho Knight
shii_cho_knight.description: Shii-Cho is the first form taught, built from older sword traditions and stripped to essentials. Its practitioners skip the flourishes and drill block, parry, and strike until the fundamentals hold under any conditions. That grounding pairs with real athleticism, so a Shii-Cho Knight both avoids an attack and answers it while the opponent is still off balance.

ship_captain.name: Ship Captain
ship_captain.description: For a Ship Captain the vessel and the crew are the whole of it. They demand a great deal from everyone aboard and give leadership in return, and a crew that stays becomes something close to family. Most captains rebel against the Empire eventually, either because its human-centric policies are intolerable aboard a mixed crew or because it threatens the independence they fly for.

shipwright.name: Shipwright
shipwright.description: Shipwrights design, maintain, and rebuild the Alliance's ships, mostly out of donations, smuggled hulls, and scrapyard rescues. The first decision on any arrival is whether it can be used, stripped, or written off. Rebel shipyards are hidden, remote, or mobile, often all three, so the work happens under the standing possibility of a rapid evacuation.

skip_tracer.name: Skip Tracer
skip_tracer.description: Skip Tracers find people who owe money and persuade them to settle, ideally without drawing a weapon. Property damage and medical bills come out of the commission, after all. The work is investigative first, chasing a trail across whatever distance it runs, and only turns to pressure when a target proves unwilling. Most Skip Tracers are considerably better at conversation than the profession suggests.

sleeper_agent.name: Sleeper Agent
sleeper_agent.description: Sleeper Agents hold a lie together for years. They take an ordinary job with peripheral access to something the Rebellion wants, then wait, sometimes for so long that the cover becomes more familiar than the identity underneath it. The hardest part is not the deception but the attachments: an agent who builds real friendships among the enemy will eventually betray them.

slicer.name: Slicer
slicer.description: For a Slicer a computer is a puzzle with a prize attached. With nearly everything in the galaxy connected to something, they are valuable people to know and dangerous ones to cross, and their worth is measured almost entirely in reputation. A group without one is at a real disadvantage the first time it needs data it was not given.

soresu_defender.name: Soresu Defender
soresu_defender.description: Soresu Defenders have mastered staying alive. Where a Protector shields others, a Soresu Defender holds ground against hordes or sustained blaster fire and simply does not fall, relying on the Force to guide the blade close to precognition. The techniques can be learned by anyone with the discipline, but only a Force-sensitive practitioner reaches what the form is actually for.

squadron_leader.name: Squadron Leader
squadron_leader.description: Squadron Leaders command the snubfighters, gunships, and hovertanks that do most of the daily fighting. They know their machines, fly the same craft as the people they lead, and are usually first into an engagement and last out of it. The role runs on example rather than rank, and the Alliance watches constantly for anyone capable of it.

starfighter_ace.name: Starfighter Ace
starfighter_ace.description: Starfighter Aces fly craft whose shields and armour mean nothing against the capital ships they attack, and trust the Force to cover the difference. Flying a single-seat fighter means handling weapons and navigation at once, under sustained physical strain, while waiting for the one instant an opponent is exposed. It is exhausting work that looks effortless from outside.

steel_hand_adept.name: Steel Hand Adept
steel_hand_adept.description: Steel Hand Adepts fight with nothing in their hands and win anyway. Unarmed traditions across the galaxy run from formal schools to improvised styles learned in cantina brawls, and an Adept draws on the Force to do what neither could manage alone: breach heavy armour, close range that should be safe, and disarm opponents who thought a weapon settled the matter.

strategist.name: Strategist
strategist.description: Strategists set the direction of the war rather than fighting it. They study the whole board, past and projected, and watch logistics closely enough to notice when a unit is stretched too thin to survive contact. The detail matters absolutely, since a forgotten item in a planetary strike costs lives in the thousands, and reading a feint correctly can save as many.

survivalist.name: Survivalist
survivalist.description: Survivalists work the places people go when they do not want to be found, which is most of the galaxy once cities and space lanes are subtracted. They keep themselves and their companions alive in country that would kill an unprepared team, and they know what to look for when hunting almost anything. They still like credits as much as anyone, and hire out accordingly.

tactician.name: Tactician
tactician.description: Victories mean nothing if nobody holds the ground afterwards, and a Tactician is who holds it. A handful of troops with the right plan can disable an installation or collapse a defensive grid, and Tacticians provide the leadership that makes that work. They insist on being able to fight unarmed if it comes to that, and the Alliance promotes them from the field constantly.

teacher.name: Teacher
teacher.description: Teachers decide that passing knowledge on serves the galaxy better than using it themselves. Their training may be classical, academic, or entirely self-taught; what matters is the ability to bring others up. Some work with schools and academies far from Imperial attention, others need nothing but a clearing and a student, and many arrive at the role because circumstance handed it to them.

thief.name: Thief
thief.description: Thieves get into places that are closed, take what they were not meant to have, and leave without leaving a trace. Selling it well afterwards makes the day. Most either work with a crew that shares the ambition or work alone, and in a mixed group a Thief may never mention the specialisation at all, since a Smuggler's general skills cover the same ground in conversation.

trader.name: Trader
trader.description: Traders look at a newly discovered world and see resources, and at an isolated community and see customers. They build connections between the Core and the far reaches, usually arriving educated in economics and politics, and they route around the restrictions that stop other people. In a group the Trader is the public face and the one who turns salvage into credits.

trailblazer.name: Trailblazer
trailblazer.description: Trailblazers give an outnumbered army the one advantage it can still hold, which is knowing the ground. Imperial forces think rigidly about terrain, and a Trailblazer exploits that with traps, ambushes, and routes the enemy assumes are impassable. Walkers do not work in dense forest and infantry surges do not work in a city, and a Trailblazer makes sure the fight happens there.

vanguard.name: Vanguard
vanguard.description: Vanguards go first. They rarely command in any formal sense, but hitting hard and early means allies fall in behind them, and the risk that comes with the position is why surviving Vanguards are extremely tough. Standing still on a battlefield dominated by walkers and orbital fire is fatal, so they keep moving and end engagements before the enemy has finished starting one.

warden.name: Warden
warden.description: Wardens take responsibility for punishing those who abuse power, which is thankless work under a regime built on it. Where other Guardians shield allies, a Warden weakens enemies, restricting their movement, wearing them down, and frightening them into stopping. Intimidation used that steadily has consequences for a character's own morality, and Wardens generally know it.

warleader.name: Warleader
warleader.description: Warleaders win fights with judgement rather than prowess. They read a battlefield instinctively, aided by the Force, and turn that into plans that look prescient from the other side. Their allies trust them for reliability rather than speeches; a Warleader keeps people out of the line of fire, finds the weakness in an enemy's plan, and gets the group home.

tor_acolyte.name: Acolyte
tor_acolyte.description: Every Sith begins here. Acolytes have found the dark side and are learning to use what it offers, reaching for their own anger and fear deliberately, as tools rather than accidents. The training rewards ambition and punishes hesitation, which is the point: an Acolyte who survives it arrives at real power already certain that feeling is something to spend.

tor_blademaster.name: Blademaster
tor_blademaster.description: Blademasters are the Sith order's soldiers. The lightsaber is their study, but their training covers most battlefield weapons, and they fight at the front in heavy armor where the Empire's lines meet the Republic's. They tend to command as well as fight. Scars are worn as evidence of commitment, and many carry cybernetics in place of what the work cost them.

tor_lord.name: Lord
tor_lord.description: A Sith Lord has done something the Empire cannot ignore. The title is granted rather than claimed, and it carries both deference and access: Lords are told more of the order's secrets, including writings that describe what the dark side will do for someone prepared to ask. Rank is also exposure, since everything a Lord has learned is worth taking from them.

tor_sorcerer.name: Sorcerer
tor_sorcerer.description: Sorcerers are the order's scholars, reading the Force out of ancient texts and the tombs and holocrons of Sith long dead. Their other study is alchemy, which is where the reading stops being theoretical: a Sorcerer can reshape living things, and put forbidden strength into an ally willing to carry it. What they know is genuinely dangerous, most reliably to whoever is standing nearby.

tor_cartel_dealer.name: Cartel Dealer
tor_cartel_dealer.description: Cartel dealers sell, smuggle and source, and they know every black market worth knowing. Most work under the Hutt Cartel, which stays deliberately neutral between the Empire and the Republic and is tolerated by both, on a reputation solid enough that few authorities want the trouble of enforcing the law on one of its members. The protection is conditional on being profitable. A dealer who stops earning finds out how conditional.

tor_gladiator.name: Gladiator
tor_gladiator.description: Gladiators fight for an audience. In some places that is a regulated profession; in others it is what happens to slaves and prisoners, and surviving it is the only way out. Those who get out sell the skill on as enforcers, mercenaries and bounty hunters. The arena teaches more than violence, though, since a fighter who cannot work a crowd does not last, so many leave it as convincing talkers as well as dangerous ones.

tor_mandalorian_crusader.name: Mandalorian Crusader
tor_mandalorian_crusader.description: The Crusaders are among the largest Mandalorian orders of the Cold War and the Galactic War, powerful enough to steer events on Mandalore and the worlds Mandalorians have settled. They are also the order outsiders notice first, and then mistake for all of them. This specialization fits most warriors raised to Mandalorian custom during the war, whatever clan or alliance they actually answer to.

tor_imperial_loyalist.name: Imperial Loyalist
tor_imperial_loyalist.description: Imperial Loyalists came up through the academies, drilled into obedience and taught that the Empire is worth dying for. Most of them believe it. That belief coexists comfortably with the service's other habit: officers advance by arranging the failure of their rivals, and blame travels down the chain far more easily than it travels up. A Loyalist is trained to fight and practiced at both.
